newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Rostelekom 1996 pre-tax 1.11 trln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Rostelekom 1996 pre-tax 1.11 trln rbls.

text.p: NOTES -- Figures prepared to Russian standards on a cash basis except for those marked with an asterisk (*), for which no basis of accounting was specified.
AOOT Mezhdugorodnoi i Mezhdunarodnoi Elektricheskoi Svyazi Rostelekom plans to publish accounts audited to international standards by auditors Coopers & Lybrand.

Rostelekom posted 2.36 trillion roubles 1995 pre-tax profit ($509 million at the January 1996 exchange rate of about 4640 roubles per dollar) and 1.15 trillion roubles net profit ($247 million) calculated to international standards.
Preliminary estimates released earlier this year put 1996 net profit to international standards at $265 million and sales around $2.0 billion after $1.78 billion (8.27 trillion roubles).
The Russian government owns 38 percent in Rostelekom, and is transferring its stake to holding company Svyazinvest.
Russian accounting standards differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities.
Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
